claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, could you tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Do you currently live in the UK with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK with Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. A few more questions:

Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex - meaning you're the one who looks after them day-to-day and pays for their food, clothes, and other needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now. So they're not living with me at the moment - they're in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. This is an important detail for determining eligibility. 

Can you tell me:

1. How long has Alex been in local authority care? (You mentioned a few months - could you be more specific about how many weeks or months?)

2. Does Alex come home to stay with you for any regular periods, such as weekends or school holidays?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in care for about 12 weeks now. And actually, I'm not entirely sure about how often they come home - sometimes they do spend time with me, but I couldn't give you an exact number of hours per week. It varies quite a bit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful for understanding your situation.

A few more questions:

1. When Alex does spend time with you, roughly how often does this happen? For example, is it most weekends, once a month, or less frequently?

2. Do you regularly spend money on Alex - such as buying them clothes, presents, food, pocket money, or contributing financially toward their care? If so, approximately how much would you say you contribute?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
When Alex does come home, it really does vary - sometimes it's more frequent, sometimes less. I honestly can't pin down a regular pattern.

As for spending money on them, no, I'm not currently contributing financially towards their needs or care. I haven't been able to help out with costs like clothes or pocket money while they've been in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your circumstances. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation:

When a child goes into local authority care for more than 8 weeks, Child Benefit usually stops. Alex has been in care for 12 weeks, which exceeds this 8-week limit.

There are exceptions that can allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit even after 8 weeks:
- If the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you, OR
- If you regularly spend money on the child (contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment would be)

In your case, you've mentioned that Alex's visits home vary and you can't identify a regular pattern of at least 24 hours per week, and you're not currently making financial contributions toward Alex's upkeep.

Based on these circumstances and the Child Benefit rules, unfortunately you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: However, if your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex starts spending regular time at home (at least 24 hours per week) or if you begin making regular financial contributions toward their care - you may become eligible again. In that case, you should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and has been in local authority care for 12 weeks. According to Child Benefit rules, when a child is in care for more than 8 weeks, Child Benefit payments usually stop. The claimant can continue to receive Child Benefit after 8 weeks only if: (1) the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home, or (2) the claimant regularly spends money on the child equivalent to at least the Child Benefit amount. In this case, the claimant confirmed that Alex's visits home vary without a regular pattern of at least 24 hours per week, and the claimant is not making any financial contributions toward Alex's upkeep. Therefore, neither exception applies, and the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
